beeTeamCoordinatesAIAgentsWorking: Bee Team coordinates AI agents working on separate tasks at the same time. Each worker keeps its own chat. The board holds the plan and the decisions that affect the team.
aBuildWorkerCanUncoverAn: A build worker can uncover an issue while another worker drafts release notes. If that finding stays in one chat, the notes can describe a release that never passed. Recording it on the task gives the lead a precise result to share.
yourHarnessRunsTheAgentsThe: Your harness runs the agents. The lead agrees on the work and assigns tasks. Workers use the references relevant to their sessions and record progress or blockers. This lets them work concurrently and retrieve decisions without replaying every chat.
beeTeamIsFreeToUse: Bee Team is free to use and intended for open-source distribution. Your harness and model provider have their own pricing. Consult the repository for the current software license and separate brand terms.
checkTheServiceIdentityAndVersion: Check the service identity and version before connecting or upgrading.
thePanelNeedsAMatchingApp: The panel needs a matching app version. Update the older component if the versions differ. A newer release for an already matching local pair is optional. Back up your data, use the verified package for your OS and recheck the version after restarting.
mcpConnectsYourHarnessToThe: MCP connects your harness to the Bee Team service over Streamable HTTP. An agent can read the board or record a decision through the same business rules as the panel.
afterInitializationTheClientDiscoversToo: After initialization, the client discovers tools, resources and prompts. Tools perform operations, resources expose bundled materials, and prompts prepare task context. Discover what the running version actually advertises.
useBeeTeamToCallListBoards: Use Bee Team to call listBoards and show my boards.
anEmptyCollectionIsValidFor: An empty collection is valid. For a write, inspect the tool schema for the declared actor, expected version and idempotency key. Actor metadata records authorship. If the version is stale, read the current record before deciding whether to retry.
beeTeamStoresWorkRecordsLocally: Bee Team stores work records locally by default. Chats run in your harness.
theServiceCreatesTheDatabaseIn: The service creates the database in the current user's home directory
startTheServiceWithTheSame: Start the service with the same data location after an upgrade. Use portable export for a supported snapshot; restore only into an empty destination.
forPostgreSQL18SetDATABASEURL: For PostgreSQL 18+, set DATABASE_URL to the dedicated database and optionally set DATABASE_DRIVER=postgres. An explicit driver must match the URL. Changing the connection selects a different store; moving existing data requires a transfer.
startWithTheSymptomYouCan: Start with the symptom you can observe.
checkHealthOnTheConfiguredPort: Check /health on the configured port from the same machine. Start the intended binary, then allow the browser's local network request if prompted.
aToolOrSkillIsMissing: A tool or skill is missing
verifyTheMCPEndpointAndClient: Verify the MCP endpoint and client scope. Refresh the harness, list the discovered skills, and check the same project directory where they were installed.
checkTheOSAndCPUIf: Check the OS and CPU. If the matching release has no verified archive, use the source-build instructions.
thePanelAsksForAnUpdate: The panel asks for an update
compareTheVersionFromApiV1: Compare the version from /api/v1/info with the open panel. Restart after updating and reload the panel.
runTheServiceOnTheComputer: Run the service on the computer where your agents work. Select the OS and CPU for that machine.
compareTheArchiveSizeAndSHA: Compare the archive size and SHA-256 before extracting the executable into a new folder.
aVerifiedArchiveForThisVersion: A verified archive for this version and platform is unavailable here. Build from source using the steps below.
fromACheckoutOfTheMatching: From a checkout of the matching release, install Rust 1.94+, Node.js 22.20+ with npm, and native build tools. Use MSVC and the Windows SDK on Windows, Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, or a C toolchain on Linux.
theExecutableIsWrittenToTarget: The executable is written to target/release. Node.js is only needed for this build.
runTheBinaryDirectlyForAPI: Run the binary directly for API and MCP. To also serve the panel, use the command below from the repository root. For an extracted download, use its executable path instead.
setupBeeTeamHandlesInstallationAnd: Setup Bee Team handles installation and updates. Get a Team Lead coordinates the team. Get a Worker starts each worker in its own chat. Use packages from the same trusted revision as your app.
forASourceInstallationRunThis: For a source installation, run this from the matching Bee Team checkout in a fresh project scope:
selectAHarnessForItsCommand: Select a harness for its command. For another client, install all three complete skill directories using its supported discovery mechanism.
refreshTheHarnessAndConfirmAll: Refresh the harness and confirm all three names appear.
checkTheInstallationAndConfirmThe: Check the installation and confirm the local API version.
chooseYourHarnessAboveToSee: Choose your harness above to see what to paste.
connectAHarnessRunningOnThe: Connect a harness running on the same computer as the Bee Team service. Each client has its own registration scope.
startBeeTeamCheckExistingRegistrations: Start Bee Team, check existing registrations, then add the connection once. Replace the port or path if you changed the defaults.
inYourClientSMCPSettings: In your client's MCP settings choose Streamable HTTP and enter
inTheDialogEnterBeeteamSelect: In the dialog enter beeteam, select HTTP, and enter the endpoint
discoverTheBeeTeamToolsAnd: Discover the Bee Team tools and call listBoards. Show the names of my boards.
anEmptyListIsASuccessful: An empty list is a successful read on a new installation.
prepareAReleaseWithTwoWorkers: Prepare a release with two workers. One writes the release notes while the other checks the build.
createAReleaseTeamForThis: Create a release team for this checkout and a board to track it. I want two workers: Release Notes and Build Verification. Confirm their profiles and team memberships.
useTheFirstPromptInThe: Use the first prompt in the notes chat and the second in the build chat. Have the lead verify both identities before assigning work.
registerAsTheReleaseNotesWorker: Register as the Release Notes worker in the release team selected by the lead. Return my agent and team IDs and wait for assignment.
registerAsTheBuildVerificationWorker: Register as the Build Verification worker in that release team. Return my agent and team IDs and wait for assignment.
giveEachWorkerADeliverableIt: Give each worker a deliverable it can complete independently. Put the shared decisions on the board.
createTwoTasksInTheRelease: Create two tasks in the release board for this checkout. Ask Release Notes to draft the changes and known limitations. Ask Build Verification to record the commit tested, command, platform and outcome. Send each worker its task and comment IDs.
openBothAssignedChatsEachWorker: Open both assigned chats. Each worker checks its task, records its execution and posts results there. The notes worker can draft confirmed changes while the build runs.
reviewRecordedEvidenceOnTheBoard: Review recorded evidence on the board, even when the workers ran in different sessions.
ifTheBuildFailsRecordThe: If the build fails, record the failed command on the build task. Link that result from the notes task so the worker can qualify the release notes without copying the whole conversation.
compareTheReleaseNotesWithThe: Compare the release notes with the recorded build result. Link the evidence and tell me which items are ready for acceptance and which need another pass.
openEachTaskToSeeIts: Open each task to see its executor, plan, latest summary and recorded decisions.
selectAndCopy: Select and copy the text above.
